items.original_text: Filing step: Request a written determination from SF Planning confirming whether Planning Code § 249.60 permits a Type 42 license transferred from outside the Mission SUD or requires an intra-SUD transfer. What to say: Submit a letter to the Planning Department's Zoning Administrator citing Planning Code § 249.60 and describing the concept as a wine bar seeking to transfer an ABC Type 42 license. Ask whether the SUD's intra-district transfer rule applies only to Type 48 (full-liquor bar) licenses or also to Type 42 (beer-and-wine bar) licenses. Request a written Zoning Determination or interpretation before filing the CUA. If the answer is that only intra-SUD transfers are allowed, identify available Type 42 licenses within the SUD through an ABC license broker before proceeding.

items.original_text: Estimated time: 210 to 540 days. Estimated government cost: $8,500 to $35,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog), followed by the ABC Type 42 license (60–150 days, or 90–240 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding or protest adds time), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days). The building permit with change of use runs in parallel after CUA approval (14–120 days for plan review). Minimum timeline assumes an uncontested CUA decided in 4 months, an unprotested ABC application in 2 months, and a POE permit in 1.5 months, totaling roughly 7 months. items.original_text: Estimated time: 210 to 540 days. Estimated government cost: $8,500 to $35,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog), followed by the ABC Type 42 license (60–150 days, or 90–240 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding or protest adds time), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days). The building permit with change of use runs in parallel after CUA approval (14–120 days for plan review). Minimum timeline assumes an uncontested CUA decided in 4 months, an unprotested ABC application in 2 months, and a POE permit in 1.5 months, totaling roughly 7 months. Maximum timeline assumes a CUA with one continuance (10 months), ABC with PCN referral and protest (8 months), and a contested POE hearing (4 months), totaling 18+ months if stages are sequential. The $3,100 CUA base fee, $2,708 POE fee, $1,000–$1,600 ABC fee, $828–$2,207 DPH plan check, $470 health permit, and $800–$15,000 building permit sum to roughly $8,500–$35,000 in government fees (construction cost determines the building permit fee). If an intra-SUD Type 42 license must be purchased from another bar, add $50,000–$150,000 (estimated, as Type 42 market prices in the Mission SUD are not published) and 90–180 days for escrow and transfer, making the true minimum timeline 12–15 months and total upfront cost $60,000–$185,000.

verdicts.supported_text: Estimated time: 210 to 540 days. Estimated government cost: $8,500 to $35,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog), followed by the ABC Type 42 license (60–150 days), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days). The building permit with change of use runs in parallel after CUA approval (14–120 days for plan review). Minimum timeline assumes an uncontested CUA decided in 4 months, an unprotested ABC application in 2 months, and a POE permit in 1.5 months, totaling roughly 7 months. Maximum timeline assumes a CUA with one continuance (10 months), ABC with PCN referral and protest (8 months), and a contested POE hearing (4 months), totaling 18+ months if stages are sequential. The $3,100 CUA base fee, $2,708 POE fee, $1,000–$1,600 ABC fee, $828–$2,207 DPH plan check, $470 health permit, and $800–$15,000 building permit sum to roughly $8,500–$35,000 in government fees (construction cost determines the building permit fee).

Basis: Planning Code § 249.60 states that good-neighbor operating conditions per § 202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits apply to all alcohol establishments in the Mission SUD. These are standard conditions in Mission SUD alcohol approvals.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: The CUA and ABC license will remain valid only so long as the use operates as a bona fide eating place serving food during all hours alcohol is served, and minors will not be permitted on the premises under ABC Type 42 rules. Basis: ABC Type 42 is an on-sale beer-and-wine public premises license that does not require food service but prohibits minors. The catalog notes that nearly every city treats Type 42 as a bar use requiring conditional use, and Planning may condition approval on continued food service to distinguish the concept from a pure bar.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Request a written determination from SF Planning confirming whether Planning Code § 249.60 permits a Type 42 license transferred from outside the Mission SUD or requires an intra-SUD transfer. What to say: Submit a letter to the Planning Department's Zoning Administrator citing Planning Code § 249.60 and describing the concept as a wine bar seeking to transfer an ABC Type 42 license. Ask whether the SUD's intra-district transfer rule applies only to Type 48 (full-liquor bar) licenses or also to Type 42 (beer-and-wine bar) licenses. Request a written Zoning Determination or interpretation before filing the CUA. If the answer is that only intra-SUD transfers are allowed, identify available Type 42 licenses within the SUD through an ABC license broker before proceeding.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, requesting authorization for a bar use (Planning Code § 303) and a change of use from restaurant to bar. What to say: Describe the concept as a neighborhood wine bar serving beer and wine with a limited menu of small plates prepared in a code-compliant kitchen, closing by 1:00 AM, with occasional live acoustic music. Emphasize that the use will operate as a bona fide eating place serving food during all hours alcohol is served, that the 1:00 AM close is within the principally permitted 6 AM–2 AM window, and that the applicant commits to the Mission SUD's good-neighbor conditions under Planning Code § 202.2. Include a Security Plan, a narrative explaining how the concept serves the neighborhood's convenience and necessity given the corridor's walkable density, and letters of support from the neighborhood association and nearby businesses. Frame live music as a secondary, accessory cultural amenity. Submit the CUA before or in parallel with lease execution, with a contingency that the lease is void if th…
outcomes.note: Records cite § 762 for bar CUA, not § 303; don't require Security Plan or specify how to describe the concept or what supporting materials to include.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Attend the pre-application community meeting required by Planning, and conduct voluntary outreach to the Mission neighborhood association, upstairs residential tenants, and SFPD Mission Station before the CUA hearing. What to say: Present the concept, operating hours, Security Plan, and soundproofing measures at the community meeting. Ask for feedback and incorporate reasonable requests into the CUA application as voluntary conditions (e.g., weeknight entertainment cutoff, complaint hotline, quarterly community meetings). Document the outreach in writing and submit meeting notes and sign-in sheets as exhibits to the CUA application. The catalog warns that sound complaints from upstairs residents are the main POE denial risk; pre-meeting neighbors and offering mitigation reduces that risk.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If the CUA is approved, immediately file the ABC Type 42 application with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, including the CUA approval, a signed lease, the seller's permit, and proof of entity registration. What to say: Submit the ABC application online with the approved CUA motion, the signed lease or letter of intent, the CDTFA seller's permit, the SOS entity registration, and the $1,000–$1,600 application fee. Post the 30-day public notice at the premises the day ABC confirms receipt. If Planning required an intra-SUD license transfer, attach the executed purchase agreement with the transferring bar and file both the person-to-person and premises-to-premises transfer applications. Notify ABC that the address is in a high-density census tract and that a Public Convenience or Necessity finding may be required; ask whether the City's CUA approval satisfies that requirement or whether a separate Board of Supervisors referral is needed. Budget 90–150 days if a PCN or protest is filed.
outcomes.note: Records show fee $1,000–$1,600, prerequisites, and that PCN may be required at this density; they don't mention 30-day notice, intra-SUD transfers, census tract classification, or 90-day minimum timeline.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Entertainment Commission Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit application, depending on the performance format and hours confirmed with EC staff. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director describing the live music program (solo/duo acoustic or amplified, performance area size, frequency, end time) and ask whether a Limited Live Performance permit or a full Place of Entertainment permit is required. If POE, file the application online with the $2,708 fee (FY 2026–27), the CUA approval, the signed lease, the Security Plan, and an acoustic report if sound is a concern. Post the 30-day yellow notice at the premises and conduct the required neighbor notification. At the hearing, commit to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy, sound-level monitoring, and a complaint log shared with the Commission. If LLP, file with the $612 fee and a reduced notice period.
outcomes.note: Record mentions only POE permit, not Limited Live Performance permit as an alternative, and doesn't specify online filing, Security Plan, hearing commitments, or LLP details.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check application for the limited kitchen, including scaled drawings, equipment specs, menu, and finishes schedule. What to say: File two sets of plans online through the DPH portal showing the kitchen layout, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, food-prep surfaces, refrigeration, and limited cooking equipment (panini press, soup warmer, etc.). Include interior and exterior photos, a menu describing small plates and reheating, and the food safety manager's ServSafe certificate. Pay the $828–$1,241 plan-check fee (FY 2026–27). Schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% construction completion and a final inspection at 100%, booking each at least two weeks in advance with the assigned plan reviewer.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements and change of use, routed through Planning, DPH, SFFD, and PUC. What to say: Submit stamped architectural, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical plans showing the bar build-out, kitchen equipment, hood and suppression system, ADA restrooms, and finishes. Mark the application as a change of use from restaurant to bar and attach the approved CUA motion. Route the permit to Planning (zoning compliance), DPH (health plan check already approved), SFFD (hood suppression and occupancy), and PUC (grease interceptor). Pay the plan-check and permit fees (percentage of construction valuation, typically $800–$15,000). Electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed subcontractors. Allow 2–4 months for full interdepartmental review.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After final DPH and Fire inspections pass, file the health permit to operate application and schedule the pre-opening DPH inspection. What to say: Submit the health permit application online with the Business Account Number, Location ID, EIN, DPH plan-check approval, and food safety manager certificate. Pay the $470 permit fee (FY 2026–27). Schedule the final inspection with the assigned inspector after construction is 100% complete, the hood suppression system is installed and certified, and the grease interceptor is in place. Walk the space against the DPH checklist (hand sinks, hot water, sealed surfaces, thermometers) one week before the inspection. The permit is issued the day the inspection passes; you cannot serve the public before it is issued.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 210 to 540 days. Estimated government cost: $8,500 to $35,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog), followed by the ABC Type 42 license (60–150 days, or 90–240 days if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding or protest adds time), and the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days). The building permit with change of use runs in parallel after CUA approval (14–120 days for plan review). Minimum timeline assumes an uncontested CUA decided in 4 months, an unprotested ABC application in 2 months, and a POE permit in 1.5 months, totaling roughly 7 months. Maximum timeline assumes a CUA with one continuance (10 months), ABC with PCN referral and protest (8 months), and a contested POE hearing (4 months), totaling 18+ months if stages are sequential. The $3,100 CUA base fee, $2,708 POE fee, $1,000–$1,600 ABC fee, $828–$2,207 DPH plan check, $470 health permit, and $800–$15,000 building permit sum to roughly $8,500–$35,000 in government fees (construction cost determines the building permit fee). If an intra-SUD Type 42 license must be purchased from another bar, add $50,000–$150,000 (estimated, as Type 42 market prices in the Mission SUD are not published) and 90–180 days for escrow and transfer, making the true minimum timeline 12–15 months and total upfront cost $60,000–$185,000.
